Usage: kagura-memory auth create-key [OPTIONS]

  Mint an API key for another workspace member (owner API key required).

  The key is printed ONCE and never persisted — save it immediately. Owner-
  provisioned keys are privilege-downgrade provisioning for member/viewer
  service identities: the server rejects self-targets and owner/admin targets.
  For your own key, use the web dashboard.

  Example:
    kagura auth create-key --user google_1234 --name ci-bot --expires-days 90

  -u, --user TEXT               Target member's user id (must hold member/viewer
                                role; not yourself)  [required]
  -n, --name TEXT               Key name (unique per workspace)  [required]
  --expires-days INTEGER RANGE  Key lifetime in days (required — never-expiring
                                provisioned keys are not allowed)  [1<=x<=3650;
                                required]
  -w, --workspace TEXT          Workspace UUID (default: the credential source's
                                workspace)
  --help                        Show this message and exit.

  Authenticate via OAuth2 device flow.

  Examples:
    kagura auth login                      # read + write (default)
    kagura auth login --read-only          # read-only
    kagura auth login --scope "memory:read memory:write profile:read"  # custom
    kagura auth login --profile work
    kagura auth login --no-browser         # for SSH / headless

  Memory scopes:

    memory:write  — create/update/delete memories, contexts, files
    (additional scopes like profile:read may be accepted server-side;
    pass them through --scope.)

  memory-cloud v0.83.0+ emails the account's verified address on every device-
  flow approval (no opt-out), so an approval you did not start shows up there.

  --profile TEXT          Profile name to store credentials under (default:
                          'default').
  --server TEXT           Server URL (default: $KAGURA_MCP_URL base, or
                          https://memory.kagura-ai.com).
  --scope TEXT            OAuth scope (default: 'memory:read memory:write').
                          Override only if you need a custom scope set.
  --read-only             Request read-only scope ('memory:read') instead of the
                          default read+write.
  --no-browser            Don't try to open a browser — just print the URL and
                          code.
  --invite LINK_OR_TOKEN  Sign up with an invite: the
                          https://<host>/join/<token> link you were sent, or its
                          bare token. Checked locally; never stored.
  --help                  Show this message and exit.

Usage: kagura-memory auth refresh [OPTIONS]

  Rotate ``access_token`` (optionally requesting a new scope).

  Examples:
    kagura auth refresh
    kagura auth refresh --scope "memory:read"                       # narrow to read-only
    kagura auth refresh --scope "memory:read memory:write"          # widen (triggers device flow)
    kagura auth refresh --profile work

  Memory scopes:
    memory:read   — read memories, contexts, files
    memory:write  — create/update/delete memories, contexts, files
    (additional scopes like profile:read may be accepted server-side;
    pass them through --scope.)

  A refresh token works once (memory-cloud v0.79.0+). The refresh is shared with
  `kagura-mcp` and KaguraClient: all of them refresh under one lock on
  credentials.json and re-read it first, so when one of them rotated the token
  meanwhile, this command keeps that token instead of sending the used refresh
  token again, and says so. With --scope it always asks the server, using the
  refresh token on file at that moment. A password reset revokes every OAuth
  token of the account (v0.83.0+), so a refresh after one fails; run `kagura
  auth login`.

Options:
  --profile TEXT  Profile to refresh (default: default profile).
  --scope TEXT    Request this scope (default: keep the current grant
                  unchanged). Pass space-separated values to ask for multiple
                  (e.g. 'memory:read memory:write'). If wider than the current
                  grant, re-runs the device flow.
  --help          Show this message and exit.

Usage: kagura-memory auth token [OPTIONS]

  Emit the raw ``access_token`` to stdout (for CI / scripts).

  The token will be auto-refreshed if it's within 5 minutes of expiry.
  A warning with the absolute expiry time is written to stderr.

  That refresh is shared with `kagura-mcp` and KaguraClient: all of them refresh
  under one lock on credentials.json and re-read it first, so when one of them
  already refreshed the profile, its token is printed and no second refresh
  runs.

  Security note: this token is short-lived — do not persist it to
  files or commit it. For long-lived CI, use a Kagura API key
  instead (set KAGURA_API_KEY in your secret store).

Options:
  --profile TEXT  Profile to use (default: default profile).
  --help          Show this message and exit.

  --include TEXT             Comma-separated lanes: pinned,upcoming,changes

  --format [full|index]      index: one short row per memory (server v0.115.0+);
                             full: the whole shape. Default: index below --max-
                             chars 10000, else full
  --max-chars INTEGER RANGE  Response budget in characters, 2000-100000 (below
                             10000 needs server v0.115.0+; default 20000)

Usage: kagura-memory changes [OPTIONS] SINCE

  List what changed in a context since SINCE, oldest first (server v0.93.0+).

  SINCE is ISO 8601 (naive = UTC). Events are created, updated, superseded (with
  superseded_by) and forgotten; a forgotten memory's events carry no summary.
  Page on with --cursor while has_more is true.

  Examples:
    kagura changes 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z
    kagura changes 2026-11-01 --kinds created,forgotten --limit 20
    kagura changes 2026-11-04T09:00:00Z --by-me

Options:
  -c, --context-id TEXT      Context ID (or set in .kagura.json)
  --until TEXT               Window end, exclusive (ISO 8601; default: now)
  --kinds TEXT               Comma-separated kinds:
                             created,updated,superseded,forgotten (with
                             --session-id/--by-me:
                             created,updated,forgotten,restored). Default: all
  --cursor TEXT              next_cursor of the previous page
  --limit INTEGER RANGE      Changes per page (default 50)  [1<=x<=100]
  --session-id TEXT          Only that session's writes (a session_id a write
                             returned; server v0.113.0+)
  --by-me                    Only your own writes, in any session (server
                             v0.114.0+)
  --max-chars INTEGER RANGE  Response budget in characters, 10000-100000
                             (default 20000)  [10000<=x<=100000]
  --help                     Show this message and exit.

  Prints the digest (REST, API key or OAuth profile). With --out, splices the

  with --profile / --tools / --add-tools: they decide which tool the truncation
  note names.

Usage: kagura-memory ingest [OPTIONS] SOURCE

  Ingest a URL or local file into Memory Cloud.

  Extracts structural sections from the source and creates one overview memory
  plus one memory per section, linked via declared_link edges. Heavy parsing
  dependencies are optional — install them with:

    pip install 'kagura-memory[ingest-pdf]'

  Text is extracted from documents (PDF/Office/HTML/EPUB), audio/video
  transcripts, and YouTube captions. Images embedded in a document are detected
  and counted but not yet OCR'd: a vision provider (Gemini 2.5 Flash by default)
  is configured but the orchestrator does not call describe_image() yet. Pass
  --no-vision to skip vision-provider configuration entirely.

  Examples:
    kagura ingest https://example.com/report.pdf
    kagura ingest ./report.pdf --tags "Q1,report"
    kagura ingest report.pdf --no-vision
    kagura ingest report.pdf --dry-run

  -c, --context-id TEXT           Context ID (or set in .kagura.json)
  --text-provider [claude|gemini|ollama]
                                  LLM provider for section/overview
                                  summarization.  [default: claude]
  --vision-provider [claude|gemini|ollama]
                                  Vision LLM provider for image OCR. Images are
                                  detected but not yet OCR'd (the orchestrator
                                  does not call describe_image), so this setting
                                  is currently a no-op. Pass --no-vision to skip
                                  vision-provider configuration entirely.

                                  provider).

                                  the workspace's object store. By default the
                                  source is archived to R2 and the resulting
                                  file_id is stamped on the overview memory's

                                  original bytes later.

                                  sections inherit lower.  [default: 0.7;

    kagura remember -s "Release 2.0 shipped" --content "..." --observed-at 2026-11-01
    kagura remember -s "Deploy key rotated" --content "..." --dedupe check

  interactive run offers to skip /kagura-recall and /kagura-remember, which
  duplicate its commands, asks whether to keep the SessionStart recall hook (the
  plugin has no automatic recall), and prints the plugin's settings.

  Examples:
    kagura setup claude
    kagura setup claude --profile default        # OAuth via kagura-mcp (recommended)
    kagura setup claude --profile default --scope user   # one entry for every project
    kagura setup claude --profile default --guardrails off --tool-profile core
    kagura setup claude --profile default --add-tools explore --context CTX_UUID
    kagura setup claude --api-key kagura_xxx --mcp-url http://localhost:8080/mcp/w/{workspace_id}
    kagura setup claude -y --api-key kagura_xxx --context-id my-project
    kagura setup claude --no-commands      # plugin users: its /kagura-memory:* instead
    kagura setup claude --no-auto-context  # always show full context list

Options:
  --api-key TEXT                  Kagura API key (skip prompt)
  --mcp-url TEXT                  MCP URL (skip prompt)
  --context-id TEXT               Context ID or name (skip prompt)
  --profile TEXT                  OAuth profile name (from `kagura auth login`).
                                  Writes the refresh-aware `kagura-mcp` stdio
                                  entry instead of a static API-key url.
                                  Mutually exclusive with --api-key.
  --project-dir TEXT              Project directory (default: current)
  -y, --non-interactive           No prompts, use defaults/flags
  --no-auto-context               Disable auto-select by directory name
  --scope [project|user]          Where the kagura-memory MCP entry goes.
                                  project: <project>/.mcp.json. user: every
                                  project on this machine, written with `claude
                                  mcp add-json --scope user` (needs the claude
                                  CLI); recommended with --profile when one
                                  profile serves every project. With an API key,
                                  the user-scope entry sends
                                  $KAGURA_MCP_API_KEY, which Claude Code reads
                                  when it connects: set it where Claude Code
                                  starts. A stronger scope's entry (local >
                                  project > user) hides a weaker one: setup
                                  warns, and with -y refuses to write an entry
                                  that would be hidden.  [default: project]
  --guardrails off|CONTEXT_ID     Add ?guardrails= to the upstream MCP URL
                                  (server v0.74.0+; kagura-mcp --guardrails, or
                                  the url's query for an API key). A re-run
                                  without it drops an earlier value. 'off' stops
                                  the server's guardrail digest AND removes the
                                  guardrails block from get_context_info: use it
                                  only when hooks, such as the kagura-memory
                                  plugin's, deliver guardrails. A context UUID
                                  picks that context's digest.
  --tool-profile NAME             Add ?profile=NAME to the upstream MCP URL
                                  (server v0.73.0+): the tools tools/list shows.

                                  (21 tools on 0.141.0); 'full' lists every tool
                                  (72). The server knows only these two (case-

                                  name. A profile is a view, not an
                                  authorization boundary: tools/call reaches an

                                  explore_hints need (or --tool-profile full).

                                  ignores an unknown name, and the list under a
                                  ?tools= allowlist. A re-run without it drops
                                  an earlier list.

                                  scoped tools called without context_id, so a
                                  session can skip list_contexts. An explicit
                                  context_id wins, and the default is checked
                                  like one. Unlike --context-id (the project's
                                  hooks and commands), it is a UUID.

                                  memories (default: on). --no-session-hook

Usage: kagura-memory update-memory [OPTIONS]

  Update an existing memory or upsert by external ID.

  Use --memory-id for in-place update, or --external-id for upsert.

  --details REPLACES the memory's details wholesale — the server does not deep-
  merge — so a bare --location without --merge-details drops every other details
  key (including the resource_id an --external-id upsert stores there: without
  it the next upsert of that id creates a new memory instead of replacing this
  one), and '{}' clears them. --merge-details sends --details/--location as a
  details_patch: the server merges their top-level keys over the current details
  in one call, keeps the keys they do not mention, and deletes a key given as
  null ('"location": null' too). --details-patch sends a patch you write
  yourself. On a server before memory-cloud 0.140.0 either falls back to reading
  the memory first with reference() and writing the merged object: two calls,
  not one atomic update (--expected-version still guards the write on 0.113.0+),
  and the read counts in the memory's access stats. A server before 0.82.0
  ignores the patch instead of refusing it; the command confirms that version
  first, writes the merged details in a second call, and exits 1 naming any
  other new flag that server ignored (--add-tag, --remove-tag, --expected-
  version, --observed-at). Coordinates must be JSON numbers, not strings: the
  server rejects string-typed lat/lon with a 422 by design.

  --add-tag/--remove-tag edit the stored tags without resending them, and
  --expected-version makes the update fail, writing nothing, when another edit
  landed since you read the memory.

  Examples:
    kagura update-memory -m MEM_UUID -s "updated summary"
    kagura update-memory --external-id ext-key -s "summary" --content "..." -t note
    kagura update-memory -m MEM_UUID --dismiss-supersede-candidate
    kagura update-memory -m MEM_UUID --accept-supersede-candidate
    kagura update-memory -m MEM_UUID --add-tag status:done --remove-tag status:open \
      --details-patch '{"status": "done"}' --expected-version 3
    kagura update-memory -m MEM_UUID \
      --details '{"location": {"lat": 35.68, "lon": 139.76}, "client": "acme"}'
    kagura update-memory -m MEM_UUID --merge-details \
      --location "35.68,139.76,Tokyo HQ"

Options:
  -c, --context-id TEXT           Context ID (or set in .kagura.json)
  -m, --memory-id TEXT            Memory UUID to update in-place
  --external-id TEXT              External ID for upsert lookup
  -s, --summary TEXT              Updated summary
  --content TEXT                  Updated content
  -t, --type TEXT                 Updated memory type
  -i, --importance FLOAT          Updated importance 0.0-1.0
  --tags TEXT                     Comma-separated tags (replaces the whole list)
  --add-tag TEXT                  Tag to add to the stored list, keeping the
                                  others (repeatable; not with --tags; server
                                  v0.140.0+)
  --remove-tag TEXT               Tag to remove from the stored list; one that
                                  is not there is ignored (repeatable; not with
                                  --tags; server v0.140.0+)
  --dismiss-supersede-candidate   Reject this memory's supersede_candidate
                                  suggestion (needs --memory-id; server
                                  v0.65.0+, older servers drop it silently)
  --accept-supersede-candidate    Accept this memory's supersede_candidate: the
                                  candidate is shadowed by a supersedes edge.
                                  Needs --memory-id and no field edits in the
                                  same call (server v0.126.0+)

                                  prints); else nothing is written and the
                                  current version is printed (server v0.113.0+)
